# okbase

> okbase makes a folder of markdown knowledge (an Open Knowledge Format bundle, a docs site, a wiki, an Obsidian vault) easy for AI agents to use: an MCP server and CLI with multilingual (vi/en/ja) search, metadata queries, SQL over spreadsheets, optional semantic search and fine-tuning, and Agent Skills for Claude Code and Codex. Rust, MIT OR Apache-2.0, read-only by default, no telemetry.

Agents set okbase up for the user; the user only answers questions.

1. Install (if `okbase --version` fails): `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tidusvn05/okbase/main/install.sh | sh` (add `-s -- --full` for semantic search and fine-tuning; Windows: `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tidusvn05/okbase/main/install.ps1 | iex`). Before the first release: `cargo install --locked --path crates/okbase-cli` in a clone (Rust 1.89+).
2. Run `okbase onboard` in the knowledge folder (or `okbase -b <folder> onboard`; `--json` for structured output). Do the first step, run it again, repeat until nothing is left.
3. At every ASK step, ask the user the question and wait; run only the commands of the chosen option.
4. Never add `--accept-license`, `--yes`, `--write`, `--force`, `--replace` or `--send-documents` unless the user agreed. A command that exits 3 needs consent: relay its `error.question`. Exit 4 means findings (lint errors, a rejected batch, a failed gate).
5. Finish with `okbase doctor` (a real MCP round trip), then ask the user to restart the agent session.
6. Inside Codex, its sandbox keeps `.codex/` read-only: ask the user to run `okbase agent install --codex` in their own terminal (error code `sandbox_blocked`).

To remove okbase: `okbase onboard --goal remove`.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): what okbase does, builds, fine-tuning
- [Usage](docs/usage.md): small, medium and large projects; every scenario (several bundles, several projects, shared servers, removing okbase)
- `okbase help --agent`: the agent contract (JSON, exit codes, error codes, consent rules, commands)
- `okbase embed tune guide`: fine-tuning the search model with agent-written questions

- [Design](docs/design.md): architecture and the evidence behind every default
